text: Version 3 of the notification and correspondence design is issued as Draft. No approval of the source version and no approval of this version is recorded in any source read by this work package.
why: The run records no human approval; a missing approval is treated as an assumption and the document continues in Draft rather than stopping.
read: Template and Rules v1 R8.1 and the realignment overlay D-RCV-60 (a missing status is an assumption, not a stop).
confirm: The document owner confirms or records the approval of version 3.
impact: Documentation only; nothing is built from an unapproved status.

text: The file name gives the version of the family and the metadata table gives the document's own issue number. The source is therefore version 2 of the family and version 1 of its own table, and this document is version 3. The source readings are kept in a 'Source version' row as 1, 28 October 2026.
why: The source file is named v2 while its table reads version 1 and the core properties read revision 1; one reading must be chosen so that the next version has a number and the change log a row.
read: Source metadata rows 'Version | 1' and 'Date | 28 October 2026'; source file name 'Recovery Workbench Notification and Correspondence Design v2.docx'; Template and Rules v1 R8.2 (the next version is the highest v<n> of the family plus 1).
applied_in: Metadata table, Version, Date and Source version rows; change log
confirm: The document owner confirms the version numbering of the family.
impact: One change-log row and one metadata row; no content depends on it.

text: The arc42 runtime-view structure of the source is kept. Sections 1 to 6 stay in their order and keep their numbers and their wording, and three sections are added at the end: 7 Owners and contracts, 8 Decisions, and 9 Realignment changes in version 3. Where a section needs the target, a numbered subsection is added under it (1.1, 2.1, 3.1, 4.1, 6.1).
why: The realignment needs an owner table, a decision table and a change table, and the source has no place for them; renumbering the source sections would break every reference to them.
read: Source sections 1 to 6 and its metadata row 'Structure | arc42 runtime view'; Template and Rules v1 R8.1 to R8.3.
confirm: The document owner accepts the added sections and subsections.
impact: Three added sections and five added subsections; no source section is renumbered or removed.

text: DL10 is read as answered on 5 November 2026 with answer A, 'Thai field names'. The source row and its fallback answer are kept word for word, section 6.1 records the answer, and this document adds no Thai wording.
why: The source and the Decision Log v10 differ on the subject and the answer of DL10, and a design cannot invent Thai wording for a bank notice.
read: Source section 6 row DL10; Decision Log v10 row DL10 (answer A, 2026-11-05).
confirm: The business lead with Legal and Compliance confirms the DL10 answer applies to notices.
impact: No wording is produced here; the wording work stays with the business lead and Legal.

text: Templates and merge fields are owned by P6 rwb-comms in rwb_comms, following Architecture v5 slide 41 and the Ownership Map v1. The DL28 answer of 13 November 2026, which gives them to the document module, is recorded as a conflict and is not applied.
why: R-PREC ranks Architecture v5 above the Decision Log, and the Ownership Map v1, the P6 endpoints and the P6 DB line all place the template with rwb-comms; the alternative would move the template to P5 without a source at a higher rank.
read: Rules v1 R3 (source precedence: Architecture v5 catalogue first, Decision Log fourth); Architecture v5 slide 41; Ownership Map v1 sheets Tables and Endpoints; Decision Log v10 row DL28.
confirm: The product owner reaffirms or amends DL28 before RWB-P6-AD017 is Done.
impact: The template tables, endpoints and stories stay with P6; a late change of DL28 would move three tables and two endpoints to P5.

text: The proof of delivery is held on the notice row: the barcode, the callback date and the delivery status, as the INT-14 and INT-15 field mapping already builds them. No separate proof table is created by this document.
why: Architecture v5 names the proof of delivery as P6 data but the Ownership Map v1 and the TSD give it no table, and the field mapping of the two WIN interfaces already places the barcode, the callback date and the sent type on the notice.
read: Architecture v5 slides 17 and 41; Ownership Map v1 sheet Tables; Interface Specifications v4 rows INT-14 and INT-15 and its Field mapping sheet (notice.barcode, notice.callback_date, notice.sent_type); Physical Schema v6 table notice.
confirm: The P6 DB story confirms the columns, and adds a proof table only if a later requirement needs one.
impact: One table instead of two; a separate proof table would be a delta migration in rwb_comms.

text: The verified contact point and its consent state are held by P1 rwb-source-data in contact_point_ext and are read and maintained through a P1 contract. The P6 screen maintains them through that contract and never writes rwb_source_data directly.
why: The Ownership Map v1 gives contact_point_ext to P1 and DP-01 forbids a service from writing another service's tables, while FSD P6 makes the contact repository a P6 feature and TSD P6 says reference data comes from P4.
read: Ownership Map v1 sheet Tables (contact_point_ext to P1); FSD P6 v3 A2.18; TSD P6 v2 T5.2; Rules v1 R5.5 DP-01 and DP-07.
confirm: The P1 and P6 service owners agree the contract, and the P1 API specification publishes the contact-point operation.
impact: One contract to add in P1; without it the consent check has no source of truth and the P6 screen has no write path.

text: A contact stop is read as X1 to X3, following the Temporal and Drools design, so a death (X3) holds messages and letters except statutory notices where the law requires service. The wider reading is applied and R-LIT-05 is flagged for correction.
why: The source names complaint, death and legal hold, and the Temporal and Drools design names X1 to X3, while R-LIT-05 names X1 and X2 only; the wider reading is the safer one for conduct and for the customer.
read: Source section 4, second bullet; Routing Logic v4 row R-LIT-05; Temporal and Drools Design v1 slide 8 and its notes.
confirm: The business lead corrects R-LIT-05 or confirms the X1 to X3 reading.
impact: One rule row and one hold reason; a narrower reading would let a notice reach a deceased customer's estate.

text: The approval of a notice is held by P7 rwb-decision in ApprovalWorkflow, started as a child of NoticeDispatchWorkflow with the notice as its source, and POST /notices/{noticeId}/approve of S4 is the litigation officer's decision point. A notice waits in Approved and is not written to the WIN file until the approval is decided.
why: Architecture v5 gives the child approval to P7 and names the approval consumer of NoticeGenerated, and the Ownership Map gives one endpoint of the decision to S4; the two can be read together only if P7 holds the record and S4 records the officer's decision.
read: Architecture v5 slides 14, 17 and 42; Ownership Map v1 sheet Endpoints (POST /notices/{noticeId}/approve to S4); source section 2, fourth bullet.
confirm: The P6, P7 and S4 service owners agree the approval record and the decide endpoint.
impact: One approval row per notice that needs approval; a wrong reading would leave the approval in the wrong service and the notice unblocked or blocked for ever.

text: The case-level list of notices stays a P6 responsibility, as Architecture v5 slide 17 states, and its path is settled in the P6 API specification. Until that path is published, this design reads a notice by GET /notices/{noticeId}.
why: Architecture v5 names GET /cases/{id}/notices and the Ownership Map holds no such row, so one of the two must be chosen; the case screen cannot work without a case-level read.
read: Architecture v5 slide 17 and its note; Ownership Map v1 sheet Endpoints.
confirm: The API owner publishes the case-level operation or confirms the per-notice read is enough.
impact: One endpoint row; without it the case screen makes one call per notice.

text: The partner instruction is issued by S9 rwb-partner through InstructionWorkflow and the partner portal, and the internal alert is a task and timeline entry of P3 rwb-case. rwb-comms keeps the template of the partner instruction and no record of the internal alert.
why: Neither kind leaves through a channel that Architecture v5 gives to rwb-comms, and the OUT list of rwb-comms names no partner or internal channel.
read: Architecture v5 slides 17, 41 and 42; source section 1.
confirm: The S9 and P3 service owners accept the two kinds in their scope.
impact: No table in rwb_comms for either kind; a record would be a delta story if one is later required.

text: The proof of delivery reaches the Workbench through ACE ingestion (INT-15) and is read by P1 rwb-source-data through v_ace_pod on the business date of the batch. rwb-comms matches it to the notice by barcode, writes the callback date and the delivery status and publishes EV-15 NoticeDelivered. No new event and no new job is created by this design.
why: No source names an event or a job for a proof arrival, and the reading of v_ace_pod is P1's by ADR-010; inventing an event would add a contract that no catalogue holds.
read: Interface Specifications v4 row INT-15; Architecture v5 slides 9, 17 and 44; ADR-010; Ownership Map v1 sheets Events and Jobs.
confirm: The P1, P6 and integration owners agree the read and the business-date trigger, and the P1 API publishes the proof operation.
impact: The notice period may start later than the delivery date by the batch lag; an event would shorten it at the cost of a new contract.

text: Contact times and frequency are reference data of P3 rwb-case, read through the reference-data contract (H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON), and are not held by P4. Roles and DoA stay with P4.
why: Rules v1 R3 gives reference data and LOV to P3 rwb-case by default ruling, and DP-07 names the P3 contract, while TSD P6 T5.2 names P4 for access and reference data together.
read: Rules v1 R3 default rulings and R5.5 DP-07; TSD P6 v2 T5.2.
confirm: The P3 and P4 service owners confirm the split.
impact: One contract dependency; the value itself is unchanged.

text: The Compliance approval of customer wording is recorded as a second approval of P7 rwb-decision with the template as its source, while approved_by_legal, approved_by and approved_at on the template row record the Legal approval that POST /admin/templates/{templateId}/approve writes.
why: The source requires two approvals of every template version and the target records only one; P7 already owns approvals and can hold the second without a new table.
read: Source section 3 row 'Approval'; TSD P6 T3.1 template fields and API-P6-006; Architecture v5 slide 14 (P7 approvals).
confirm: Compliance and Legal confirm the second approval and where it is recorded.
impact: One approval row per template version; without it the Compliance step is unrecorded.

text: No date of the source is moved. The source date of 28 October 2026 is kept, no release date is added by this document, and every release read from the plan is marked '(tentative)'.
why: U7 and DL48 keep the dates unchanged and tentative, and a date is never raised as a gap.
read: Rules v1 R1 U7 and R8.4 DL48; the source date line and metadata row 'Date | 28 October 2026'; split_plan.json.
applied_in: Metadata table, Date and Source version rows; section 7.2; section 8
confirm: The programme confirms the release dates at planning time.
impact: Documentation only; no schedule is committed here.

text: Every owner in this document is a service code of the Microservice Ownership Map v1 and the plan ownership file, or a party outside the 19 services (ACE Common, WIN, NSS, LINE OA). No owner is a team type and no owner is a person.
why: D-RCV-60 and U3 use soft ownership by team type in the stories and one owner per item in the technical designs; a person's name is forbidden anywhere.
read: Microservice Ownership Map v1 sheet Services; _work/msr/plan/ownership.json; Rules v1 R3, R5.3 and U3.
confirm: None needed; the map is the register of owners.
impact: No team type is named as an owner in this design.

text: The interaction ledger entry is written through the P1 contract in the same workflow step as the send, so a failed ledger write leaves the message unsent and the notice held.
why: The source requires every message to be written to the ledger but does not say in which order; writing before the send is the only order that cannot produce a sent message with no ledger entry.
read: Source section 4, fourth bullet; DP-18; R-UNI-39 (the state change and its record are one transaction); FSD P6 v3 A2.3.4.3 (a failed decision-log write on a refusal returns 503 and nothing is sent).
confirm: The P1 and P6 owners confirm the order and the failure behaviour.
impact: A P1 outage holds messages rather than losing ledger entries.
